name: tengu_amber_wren
what: The default file-read limits (maximum size, and 25,000 tokens unless CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS says otherwise) are fixed in the client. Before 2.1.268 a server config could change them.

workarounds.text: CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS sets the token limit for a file read.

name: tengu_cobalt_plinth_hazel
what: Starting a new artifact from a type in cloud sessions is decided by tengu_cobalt_plinth_larch instead of its own gate tengu_cobalt_plinth_hazel. That gate already decided artifact types.
mechanism: In 2.1.261 the cloud type-create check (offset 169493914) read CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_TYPE_CLOUD_CREATE and fell back to tengu_cobalt_plinth_hazel (default off); in 2.1.268 it (offset 173290690) falls back to tengu_cobalt_plinth_larch instead.

workarounds.text: CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_TYPE_CLOUD_CREATE replaces the gate in both directions.

name: tengu_cobalt_plinth_osier

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.268.

name: tengu_amber_stoat
what: The built-in Explore and Plan agents, and the prompts that point to them, are always registered. Before 2.1.139 a server gate, on by default, could withdraw them.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 the built-in agent list (offset 77143847) added the Explore and Plan agents only when tengu_amber_stoat (default on) was on, and the plan-mode and tool guidance mentioned them on the same condition; in 2.1.139 the same predicate (offset 189931736) returns a constant true.

workarounds.text: CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS removes the built-in agents in SDK sessions.

name: tengu_compact_line_prefix_killswitch
what: File contents shown to the model seem to always number lines in the compact form ("12<tab>text"). Before 2.1.139 a server kill switch, off by default, could bring back the padded "    12->text" form.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 the line formatter (offset 73114220) wrote the number and a tab while tengu_compact_line_prefix_killswitch (default off) was off and a six-wide number with an arrow otherwise; in 2.1.139 the formatter (offset 185866156) takes only a separator (tab, or ":" for tab-indented content) and the padded form is gone.

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.139.

name: tengu_keybindings_dom
what: Keyboard shortcuts are probably always dispatched through the newer handler registry. Before 2.1.139 a server gate, on by default, could fall back to the older per-component input handler.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 three keybinding hooks (offset 75976514) passed a no-op to the old input listener when tengu_keybindings_dom (default on) was on and their own handler otherwise; in 2.1.139 the hooks (offset 188741512) only register with the handler registry and the old listener path is gone.

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.139.

name: tengu_loud_sugary_rock
what: For claude-opus-4-7 the system prompt likely always uses the shorter text-output guidance ("Write code that reads like the surrounding code ..."). Before 2.1.139 a server gate, off by default, chose it.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 the guidance function (offset 84013521) chose the alternative guidance for opus-4-7 only when tengu_loud_sugary_rock (default off) was on; in 2.1.139 the guidance builder (offset 197002528) returns the short text for claude-opus-4-7 without a gate.

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.139.

name: tengu_mcp_retry_failed_remote
what: A remote MCP server (HTTP, SSE or claude.ai proxy) that fails its first connection with a transient error is always retried with backoff. Before 2.1.139 a server gate, on by default, could turn the retries off.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 the failed-connection handler and the startup connect (offset 82528603) both retried only when tengu_mcp_retry_failed_remote (default on) was on; in 2.1.139 the handler (offset 195456120) retries whenever a classifier calls the failure retryable and the startup connect always schedules its retry pass.

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.139.

name: tengu_miraculo_the_bard
what: Fast mode availability is always fetched from the server at startup. Before 2.1.139 a server kill switch, off by default, could skip the fetch and decide from the cached organisation flag.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 the startup prefetch (offset 86040257) called the fast mode status fetch unless tengu_miraculo_the_bard (default off) was on, in which case it set the status from penguinModeOrgEnabled; in 2.1.139 the prefetch block (offset 187009415) calls the fetch with no gate.

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.139.

name: tengu_noreread_q7m_velvet
what: The Read tool description always tells the model not to re-read a file it just edited, and Write results add that the file state is current. Before 2.1.139 a server gate, off by default, added both.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 tengu_noreread_q7m_velvet (default off) added "Do NOT re-read a file you just edited ..." to the Read description and a file-state note to the Write result (offset 75285831); in 2.1.139 both texts are added unconditionally (offset 188037609).

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.139.

name: tengu_satin_quoll
what: The server configuration of per-tool output limits (including the MCP tool output limit) moved from tengu_satin_quoll to tengu_velvet_ibis.
mechanism: In 2.1.124 the MCP output limit (offset 81451165) read MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS and then the mcp_tool entry of tengu_satin_quoll (default an empty object), and the per-tool limit table read the same config; in 2.1.139 both (offset 194350779) read tengu_velvet_ibis.

workarounds.text: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS sets the MCP tool output limit and takes precedence.

name: Grep and Glob tools hidden on native macOS and Linux builds
what: On the native macOS and Linux builds the Grep and Glob tools are no longer offered to the model by default. Searching goes through the embedded grep and find in the Bash tool instead.
mechanism: In 2.1.116 the filter that hides the two tools (offset 74645968) ran only when the environment variable EMBEDDED_SEARCH_TOOLS was set; from 2.1.117 the same filter (offset 75172207) tests a compiled-in true, so it is always on and Glob and Grep are left out of the tool list (offset 83371085). In 2.1.287 the filter sits at 185964347; the variable survives only as a registry entry (178194086) that no code reads, and both tools still report the display name "Search" (186693440). At offset 202586077 in the win32-x64 build of 2.1.278 the filter still reads process.env.EMBEDDED_SEARCH_TOOLS, so on Windows the tools stay unless that variable is set. From 2.1.117 to 2.1.160 the CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT values sdk-ts, sdk-py and sdk-cli also kept the tools; by 2.1.168 those three were dropped and an opt-in from the launch lists took their place.

workarounds.text: From 2.1.162, Grep or Glob named in --tools at launch sets the search-tools opt-in and brings both tools back for that session.
Grep or Glob named in --allowedTools at launch works the same way, because the opt-in reads the --allowedTools rules as well as --tools.
Running with CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=local-agent keeps both tools, because the filter skips that entrypoint.

changelog.quote: Native builds on macOS and Linux: the `Glob` and `Grep` tools are replaced by embedded `bfs` and `ugrep` available through the Bash tool — faster searches without a separate tool round-trip (Windows and npm-installed builds unchanged)

workarounds.text: There has been no switch for this since 2.1.69.

name: tengu_mcp_tool_search

mechanism: In 2.1.59 the mode function (offset 65237756) returned "standard" when tengu_mcp_tool_search (default on) was explicitly false and "tst-auto" otherwise; in 2.1.69 the one mode function (offset 75015076) ends by returning "tst", so the unset default moved from auto to always.

workarounds.text: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH still chooses the mode. A false value gives "standard", and "auto" or a percentage gives auto mode.
